svg.text: HARDWARE, PROGRAM, NODE: one paint each. Variants, and today's paints to compare.
As test gear: the green of an old oscilloscope's case.
Today's navy, lighter and bluer, so it no longer passes for black.
A warm red-brown, as some studio desks and amps.
Field gear: olive drab, warm and quiet.
The other way round: hardware in between, PipeWire's own nodes the light ones.
For comparison: the metal and the cream are both light, and navy passes for black.
· Lightness first: one kind light, one dark, one in between. Two of a kind's lightness is what made the metal and the cream alike.
· Then a hue only for the one in between, muted, so it doesn't fight the bands (teal, blue, green, rust, violet, plum, ochre).
· The frames stay dark on every paint: the jacks and the bands read the same on all three.
· Metal keeps its painted texture in the app (here flat), the others their noise.
